title: Four Earthquakes Shake Jammu and Kashmir in 12 Hours, No Damage Reported
excerpt: Tremors of magnitude 2.7 to 3.9 were recorded in the Doda-Kishtwar belt and in Leh on Saturday, at depths of 5 to 15 kilometres. Officials reported no loss of life or damage to property.
body:
• Four earthquakes struck Jammu and Kashmir within about 12 hours on Saturday, November 14, with epicentres in the Doda-Kishtwar belt of the Chenab Valley and one in Leh, Ladakh.
  • The tremors measured 3.3 (Kishtwar, 2:38 a.m., depth 15 km), 2.7 (Doda, 8:31 a.m., depth 10 km), 3.8 (Doda, 8:48 a.m., depth 5 km) and 2.9 (Doda, 1:09 p.m., depth 10 km); the National Center for Seismology separately recorded a 3.9-magnitude tremor in Leh at 10:29 a.m.
  • No loss of life or damage to property had been reported from anywhere in Jammu and Kashmir, officials said.
  • Large parts of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh fall in Seismic Zones IV and V, the two highest-risk categories in India's seismic zoning map.

Four earthquakes were recorded in Jammu and Kashmir within about 12 hours on Saturday, clustered in the Doda-Kishtwar belt of the Chenab Valley, officials said. None caused reported harm.

The sequence began at 2:38 a.m. with a magnitude 3.3 tremor in Kishtwar district at a depth of 15 kilometres. Two tremors followed in Doda district in the morning — magnitude 2.7 at 8:31 a.m. at a depth of 10 kilometres, and the strongest, magnitude 3.8, at 8:48 a.m. at a shallow depth of 5 kilometres. The fourth, magnitude 2.9, was recorded in Doda at 1:09 p.m. at a depth of 10 kilometres, according to data released by disaster management authorities and reported by Nawai Duggar and The Kashmir Horizon, citing the GNS news agency and independent forecaster Faizan Arif.

A fifth tremor, in Ladakh

The National Center for Seismology's account, reported by JK Express, counts the day slightly differently: of the four tremors it listed across Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh within 11 hours, three were in the Chenab Valley and one — magnitude 3.9 — struck Leh in Ladakh at 10:29 a.m. at a depth of 10 kilometres. Police said there were no reports of damage from the affected areas.

Tremors in the magnitude 2.7 to 3.9 range are minor: typically felt as a brief shaking near the epicentre, and not of a size that damages sound structures. The shallow depth of the 3.8-magnitude Doda tremor — 5 kilometres — explains why it was distinctly felt despite its modest magnitude.

Why this belt shakes often

The Chenab Valley districts of Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban sit in one of the Himalaya's active seismic belts, where the Indian plate's continued push into the Eurasian plate builds the stress that small tremors release. Large parts of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh fall under Seismic Zones IV and V in India's zoning map — the categories that building codes treat as the highest risk.

Saturday's cluster is a reminder of exposure, not a prediction. Seismologists do not treat a run of small tremors as a reliable forecast of a larger one. Officials had reported no loss of life or damage to property from anywhere in the Union Territory as of Saturday afternoon.
